> I've got a working implementation of this in [#39015](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/39015) if it's useful, behind an `experimental.auto_approve` flag.
> 
> Before anyone spends time on it, is a native version something you'd want or is the OpenGuardrails plugin the intended approach? Happy to close if latter.
> 
> Case for native: it works with no config on a default install, `deny` rules and existing `always` grants keep working, and subagent sessions are never auto-approved since a subagent's prompt is model written. In a plugin the permissions evaluation will be outside core.
> 
> I implemented it on a fork we've been using internally and it works pretty well, a little conservative but better than overly permissive `--auto`. Figured the community might find it useful.

Thanks for sharing this implementation. I think it is largely working, i had to change the rules around a little bit to fit my needs (as you mentioned it is "a little conservative"). Some additions i made also includes, reusing the model picker to set the model for reviewer model. I also rerouted `--auto` to use the review mode instead because honestly `--auto` is just a little deceptively intelligent to me when it is just approving everything.

Another macOS repro today (1.18.30), this time after **resuming a large session** rather than a fresh `opencode` launch. Same end state as the OP: blank/white TUI, no log error, keystrokes (including quit) ignored, only `kill -9` recovers.

### Repro

```sh
opencode -s ses_f37f75a4cffeL4fagJyNraDOyB
# session was already large: 8,295 parts / 124 messages / ~32k events
```

Previous instance of that session had been killed earlier (likely OOM-adjacent — see #50578). Reloading it produced:

| Observation | Value |
|---|---|
| PID state after ~10 min | `S+`, **0.1–0.5% CPU**, RSS **~2.5 GB** |
| Last log line (`run=37b3e4a4`) | `message="booting location services" directory=...` |
| ERROR / panic / WARN for that run | **none** |
| Main thread (`sample`, 2s) | blocked in **`kevent64`** (event-loop wait, not a busy spin) |
| Children | none |
| stdin | still `/dev/ttys000`, but no key handling |
| DB | `PRAGMA integrity_check` → `ok` |

Boot sequence matches this issue: config loads → `init count=56` → watcher → `booting location services` → **silence**. A healthy run of the same directory continues within ~12s to `command` / `loop` / session work; this run never got there.

### Why this repro matters

The blank freeze here is preceded by an **immediate multi-GB RSS spike on session resume** (25 MB of parts → ~2.2 GB RSS in ~33 s). Heap analysis and vmmap for that path are in #50578. Plausible link: heavy resume allocation / layout work leaves the TUI before the first paint or before the input loop is fully live, so the process sits idle in `kevent64` with nothing drawn and no keybind handling.

Related: #44337 (empty frames on Apple Silicon), #32560 / #35494 (blank startup hang), #50578 (resume RSS spike + heap snapshots).

### Environment

```
opencode: 1.18.30 (Homebrew)
os:       macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64
terminal: ghostty 1.3.1
```

Happy to re-run with `--print-logs` / take a fresh heap snapshot if that helps.

Re: the duplicate check — confirmed, and the framing here was too narrow, so I have edited the
body (and title) accordingly.

- **#50451 is the same root cause and is the stronger reproduction**: it records the transport
  status (`426`, `provider.invalid-request`) and shows the beta **CLI** failing on macOS, not
  just the desktop app. My report only covered the desktop, which made it look like a
  desktop-specific bug. Predicting variable across both reports is the `0.0.0-beta-*` channel:
  stable desktop `2.0.12` and CLI `0.0.0-dev-19977` pass, every beta build fails, and #50451
  shows that raising the beta counter (`19059` → `19271`) changes nothing.
- **#49944** reports the identical message while stating version **1.18.30**, and **#49918**
  likewise after "already updated to the latest version" (no number given, Linux). Taken at
  face value those two are clients whose version string *does* satisfy `>= 1.18.0` yet are
  still rejected, which is another indication that the label is not what is actually being
  compared. They look like a distinct sub-case from the beta-channel one, so I would not fold
  them in here.
- **#49756 / #49433** are a different failure and should not be folded in: HTTP **403** with
  `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`, on stable 1.18.31 via
  `opencode serve`, attributed to a missing `User-Agent`.

What this issue contributes beyond #50451 is the desktop-channel matrix and the negative
evidence that the gate is not in the client at all (string absent from this repo and from the
203 MB bundled `opencode-cli.exe`, while control strings match), i.e. the fix has to be
server-side. Happy to close this as a duplicate of #50451 if maintainers would rather track it
in one place — say the word and I'll do it.

opencode() {

Real-world repro on **v1.18.30 (Homebrew, macOS 26.6.2, arm64)** that matches the abort-does-not-stop-bash behavior, with an extra wrinkle: the bash commands launch **headed Chrome** via Playwright, so orphans stay visible until manually killed.

### Context

An agent session got stuck re-running the same diagnostic ~**91 times in ~92s**:

```bash
TYPESAFE_API_KEY="$TYPESAFE_API_KEY" python3 /tmp/debug_hao123_dom.py
```

Each invocation does `playwright.chromium.launch_persistent_context(headless=False, args=["--load-extension=..."])`, opens `https://www.hao123.com/`, then `context.close()`. Permission was `bash pattern=* action=allow`, so there was no human gate between retries. (The retry storm itself is agent behavior — the part I’m reporting here is **what cancel failed to do**.)

DB stats for session `ses_f3783e631ffeciay6h3VXCyL9i`:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| bash parts with that command | 91 (10:03:45 → 10:05:17 UTC) |
| status `completed` | 89 |
| status `error` | 2 |
| outputs containing `User aborted the command` | 59 |
| tool parts finalized **after** cancel timestamp | ~20+ within ~1.7s |

### Timeline (from `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`)

```
10:05:15.396  evaluated permission=bash ... python3 /tmp/debug_hao123_dom.py  (still issuing)
10:05:15.524  cancel session.id=ses_f3783e631ffeciay6h3VXCyL9i
10:05:16.475  ERROR process ... error=Aborted
10:05:16.948  cancel session.id=ses_f3783e631ffeciay6h3VXCyL9i   (second cancel)
10:05:16.958  evaluated permission=external_directory ...          (tool pipeline still active)
10:05:17.084–17.245  ~20 bash tool parts flipped to status=completed
```

So after the first `cancel` / `Aborted`:

1. Permission evaluations for in-flight tools still ran for **>1.4s**.
2. A batch of bash parts was only finalized ~**1.5s later** (many with `<shell_metadata>User aborted the command</shell_metadata>` but `status=completed`).
3. **Chrome grandchildren were not reaped.** The script’s `context.close()` never ran for aborted mid-flight runs; multiple headed Chrome instances with `--user-data-dir=/var/folders/.../T/opencode/jev-*` survived. Esc/cancel did not kill them — I had to **force-kill manually**.

### Expected

On session abort:

- immediately cancel active bash tool(s) and kill the **process group** (not just the shell parent),
- finalize tool parts promptly as aborted (not leave permission/read work running),
- no surviving Playwright/Chrome descendants under `$TMPDIR/opencode/`.

### Suspected areas

- Same family as this issue: abort ordering vs. tool Promise (#40829).
- Process-group / orphan cleanup: #20902, #30868, #3057, #29856 (closed — Chrome orphans after interrupt), #11527.
- Secondary (not the abort bug, but amplifies it): unrestricted `permission bash pattern=*` allowed a 91× headed-Chrome retry loop with no confirmation.

### Repro sketch

1. Allow `bash` with `pattern=*`.
2. Have the model run a Playwright script that does `launch_persistent_context(headless=False, ...)` and is slow/failing enough to retry in a loop.
3. While Chrome windows are popping, press Esc/Esc to abort.
4. Observe: log shows `cancel` + `Aborted`, but tool finalization lags and Chrome processes remain until manually killed.

Happy to share the full log slice / `opencode.db` extracts for the session if useful.

This issue might be related to existing issues. Please check:

- #50563: **[FEATURE]: Configurable concurrency limit for parallel tool calls within a step** — directly covers the root cause described here: the tool runner forks every tool call in one model response immediately with no bound, and Code Mode already has `TOOL_CALL_CONCURRENCY = 8` as a cap. The fix direction you describe (cap concurrent tool subprocesses) is exactly what that feature request proposes.
- #48715: **Desktop: server sidecar crashes repeatedly under memory pressure (Windows)** — same platform and general failure mode (Windows memory pressure → crash), though the specific crash path differs (`0xC0000409` / V8 heap vs. ripgrep OOM + `STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW` here).

Your report adds valuable new evidence: concrete exit-code diagnostics for the renderer crash, the tool-state leak (283 parts stuck `running`), and the permission-evaluation tight-loop observed in server logs. That makes it worth keeping open independently even if the fix overlaps with #50563.

Thanks for testing! That result actually matches the diagnosis rather than contradicting it: the socket is only killed when the body drain takes longer than the 5s keep-alive window (client slower than ~1 MB/s). A fast local client finishes the body well inside that window — that's exactly why most sessions work and only large ones on slow paths fail.

Two deterministic repros that avoid the timing lottery:

1. Throttle the client against a large session:
```
curl --limit-rate 600K -u opencode:$PW http://127.0.0.1:4990/api/session/<bigSessionId>/message
# curl: (18) transfer closed with N bytes remaining to read
# response declares content-length: 9517142
```

2. Minimal repro with no opencode code: Bun + `@effect/platform-node` returning a 9.5 MB string body to a 600 KB/s client → cut at ~9 s (~5.4 MB sent). Same server under Node completes, and chunked `HttpServerResponse.stream` under Bun completes. Setting `server.keepAliveTimeout = 0` fixes it (Bun 1.4.x, macOS arm64 — given your Windows result, platform/Bun version may matter).

The change in #50507 only disables that timer, so it's a no-op wherever the bug doesn't manifest.

Confirmed on current `v2`. The ground truth is `packages/schema/src/skill.ts:27-34`:

```ts
export const Info = Schema.Struct({
  id: ID,
  name: Name,
  description: Schema.String.pipe(optional),
  autoinvoke: Schema.Boolean.pipe(optional),
  path: AbsolutePath,
  content: Schema.String,
}).annotate({ identifier: "Skill.Info" })
```

`path` is at line 32, and `Skill.Info` has no `location` field at all. The editor takes exactly that type — `add(skill: Skill.Info): void` at `packages/plugin/src/promise/skill.ts:9` and `packages/plugin/src/effect/skill.ts:9` — so a plugin author who copies the example gets a type error and a missing required `path`, not a registered skill.

There are two occurrences, not one:

- `services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/index.mdx:817`
- `services/www/src/docs/content/build/plugins/effect.mdx:870`

Both are the same skills example — `index.mdx` uses the promise editor, `effect.mdx` wraps it in `Skill.Info.make(...)` — and in each one the `location` key is the only field that does not exist in `Skill.Info`.

Plan: rename `location` to `path` in both examples, which is the documentation fix you suggested. I would not change the `Skill.Info` shape, since accepting `location` as an alias (or making `path` optional) is a schema decision rather than a documentation defect, and `path` is what the generated `Skill.Info` reference already documents.

```yaml
mode: subagent
permission:
  edit:
    "*": deny
  bash:
    "*": deny
```

Every call to this subagent failed with `Error from provider (Console): OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`, while normal build-agent requests in the same session worked fine, matching what's reported here for `agent=compaction` / `agent=title`.

```yaml
mode: subagent
```

The root cause looks like an asymmetry between tool path resolution and the app-facing filesystem endpoint. `FileAccess.resolvePath` (`packages/core/src/file-access.ts`) already expands a leading `~` before resolving, so a model-initiated read of `~/.local/bin/gh` works (that expansion landed in #45605), while `FileSystem.Service.resolve` (`packages/core/src/filesystem.ts`) resolves the raw input with `path.resolve(location.directory, input)`. The `fs.read` request behind a pill click therefore turns `~/.local/bin` into `<location>/~/.local/bin` and reports "File not found", while the absolute form resolves.

Expanding it server-side, next to the existing resolution, seems like the right layer: the Desktop client cannot know the server home directory, and this report is exactly a Windows client against a WSL server. My plan is to make `read`/`list` reuse the same tilde handling as tool paths and add regression tests covering `~/` and the unchanged relative-path case.

Still reproducible on a fresh install. Same root cause confirmed.

**Environment**
- OpenCode Desktop: **1.18.32** (latest release as of 2026-09-22)
- OS: Windows 11 (win32, PowerShell 5.1)

**Reproduced behavior**

`open-path` runs:
```
C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe D:\OBSIDIANDATA\developer
```
and fails with `CommandNotFoundException` (CategoryInfo: ObjectNotFound), because the working directory is passed as a positional argument and PowerShell executes it as a command.

**Confirmed at the code level** - in the packaged `resources\app.asar` / `out\main\index.js` (v1.18.32):

```js
ipcMain.handle("open-path", async (_event, path, app2) => {
  if (!app2) return shell.openPath(path);
  await new Promise((resolve2, reject) => {
    const [cmd, args] = process.platform === "darwin"
      ? ["open", ["-a", app2, path]]
      : [app2, [path]];   // <- path passed as the sole argv[1]
    execFile(cmd, args, (err) => err ? reject(err) : resolve2());
  });
});
```

The renderer's Windows menu entry is `openWith: "powershell"`, so this resolves to `execFile("C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe", [path])`.

I verified the exact failure by running the same command directly:
```
powershell.exe D:\OBSIDIANDATA\developer
+ CategoryInfo : ObjectNotFound: (D:\OBSIDIANDATA\developer:String) [], CommandNotFoundException
```

This is broken on Windows by design of the `open-path` handler, independent of shell version (affects both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7).

**Note:** A fix PR is already open and awaiting review/merge: **#46712** (`cmd /d /c start` + `-EncodedCommand`/`Set-Location -LiteralPath`). Happy to retest once it lands.

Your proposal is very close to a workflow we are exploring with CPJ, an independent third-party control surface for supported local OpenCode sessions. CPJ is not built by the OpenCode team and is not affiliated with OpenCode.

We keep the OpenCode process on the user’s Windows or macOS machine and use a separate phone/web surface to view events and send follow-up input when the session exposes that capability. We are interested in the same boundaries your proposal calls out: session identity, multi-machine routing, event streaming, approval prompts, and what a gateway should or should not persist. This is not a claim of official integration or compatibility.

On our side, credentials and the full source tree stay on the execution device. Prompts, terminal output, titles, paths, and code snippets appearing in output may cross the encrypted relay. Recovery and stop actions are capability-dependent, and an accepted request is not reported as completed.
